# Overview {.unnumbered}

**Two Clocks** studies how latency-critical perception and vision-language model serving share a GPU, with a focus on deadlines, freshness, and useful throughput.

The initial question is small and concrete: can two checked workloads coexist, and does active sharing change the fast service beyond the cost of keeping both deployments resident?

::: {.callout-note title="Current evidence · 1 November 2026"}
The project is at launch validation.
The experiment chapter is planned.
:::

## Read the experiment

- [Can Two Inference Workloads Share One GPU?](experiments/r0a-pilot.qmd) explains the question, four comparison arms, proposed predictions, and the next decision.
- [Measurement Methodology](methods/measurement-methodology.qmd) defines the proposed measurement boundaries and accounting rules. Implementation and validation status remain explicit.

The first study concerns one GPU and replayed visual inputs. It can support a bounded inference-systems observation.

## How this book relates to the repository

| Record | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Experiment chapter | Question, predictions, design, amendments, observations, interpretation, and decision |
| Measurement chapter | Shared definitions and their implementation/validation status |
| Configurations, source, manifests, and raw records | The primary evidence behind each reported result |
| Diagrams | Design sketches |

Every future result will identify its run and configuration, show both services, retain unsuccessful work, and state its evidence limits.
